item.title: Optimal portfolio choice under green transition timing risk
item.description: arXiv:2610.33597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an investor's optimal portfolio choice problem when they account for the impact of a possible future green transition, whose timing is uncertain. We model the green transition as a discontinuity in the stock price processes, driven by a single jump process with constant intensity, in which 'green' stocks increase in value and 'brown' stocks decrease in value. The investor is ambiguous about the timing of the green transition and designs an investment strategy which is robust to this risk. The investor has constant relative risk aversion preferences over both wealth and model ambiguity, which introduce a multiplicative ambiguity penalty for power utility and an additive ambiguity penalty for log utility. We separate the problem into pre- and post-transition cases, derive the solution, and provide a verification theorem. We further show that the log utility, ambiguity-neutral, and worst-case problems are obtained as special cases of our general problem. In a case study with one green and one brown stock, we show that when the stock prices are positively correlated, an investor who is aware of transition risk increases their investment in the green stock and reduces their investment in the brown stock, compared to when they ignore the possibility of a transition. We illustrate the difference between an ambiguity-averse and a risk-averse investor, and show how an ambiguity-averse investor re-allocates their portfolio as their view on the probability of a green transition changes.
item.dc:creator: Emma Kroell, Mogens Steffensen

item.title: Jensen gaps and the decomposition principle
item.description: arXiv:2610.33786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide axiomatic characterizations of Jensen-gap functionals, which have the form $\rho(X)=\mathbb{E}[f(X)]-f(\mathbb{E}[X])$ for some real-valued function $f$ called the generator. This class includes important examples such as the excess growth rate, the utility premium, the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, and the variance, and is also closely related to measures of variability. We analyze various forms of convexity for Jensen gaps. To characterize Jensen gaps, we formulate conditional versions of law-invariant functionals, which are needed to state the decomposition principle. On an atomless probability space, we show that law invariance together with a binary decomposition principle is sufficient to characterize Jensen gaps on simple random variables. Under suitable continuity conditions, the characterization extends to broader classes, including compactly supported random variables and integrable random variables. We then identify the generator $f$ by imposing either of two natural invariance conditions: scaling invariance or translation invariance. The former identifies logarithmic, $x\log x$, and power generators, whereas the latter identifies exponential and quadratic generators.
item.dc:creator: Lilian Hu, Ruodu Wang

item.title: Optimal ratcheting dividend policies with resets
item.description: arXiv:2610.34348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an optimal dividend policy problem under ratcheting and bankruptcy constraints. Firms face a tradeoff between the negative signal of a dividend reduction and a potential future bankruptcy. In contrast to previous works, the dividend rate is allowed to decrease after incurring a negative impact on equity valuation in accordance with a large empirical literature on the topic. We provide an explicit necessary and sufficient condition for the finiteness of the value function and prove the differentiability of the value function, and its characterization via viscosity solutions and the so-called supercontact property. The value function is given by the solution of a two-dimensional variational inequality combining optimal stopping, singular and impulse controls. We show that the problem is equivalent to a one-dimensional setup simplifying both mathematical and financial analysis. Finally, we provide a numerical study of the model and a sensitivity analysis with respect to the model parameters. We show the relevance of over-reaction to financial news on the manager's optimal policy.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Roch, Simone Scotti

item.title: Martingality in EFM Signature Volatility Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.35022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a martingality criterion for the Exponentially Fading Memory (EFM) signature volatility model, extending the recent result of Abi Jaber, Gassiat, and Sotnikov (2026). In the proposed framework, the volatility process is given by a linear functional of the EFM signature of a time-augmented Brownian motion, which yields a globally well-behaved, fully non-Markovian volatility model admitting a stationary distribution. The stationary EFM signature volatility model is also covered by allowing for a random initial value of the signature. Moreover, the volatility process can be adjusted to the initial forward variance curve. For this model, excluding trivial cases, we prove that the price process is a true martingale if and only if the truncation order is odd and a sign condition involving the correlation parameter holds.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Sotnikov, Adeline Viot

item.title: A Stationary Mean-Field Model for Carbon Market Stability Reserve
item.description: arXiv:2610.33132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the design of a market stability reserve as a stationary mean-field singular control problem. The allowance balance follows a regime-switching diffusion, while the regulator injects or withdraws allowances through bounded-variation controls. The objective trades off the average allowance balance, its stationary dispersion, deviations from a long-run target, and intervention costs. The optimal policy is a regime-dependent band rule characterized by four reflecting thresholds. Its computation reduces to a scalar fixed-point problem combining a coupled variational inequality with the invariant distribution of the reflected process. A calibration to the EU ETS yields thresholds of the same order of magnitude as the existing Market Stability Reserve rule. Comparative statics show that volatility is the main determinant of the intervention band, whereas the frequency and duration of crisis regimes have limited effects. A simpler two-threshold policy based on average regime dynamics closely reproduces the optimal regime-dependent policy in terms of liquidity and intervention volumes.
item.dc:creator: Ren\'e A\"id, Federico Cannerozzi, Giorgio Ferrari

item.title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic H\"older estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Chassagneux, St\'ephane Cr\'epey, Gr\'egoire Loeper, Justin Ruelland

item.title: Fourier-Laplace transforms in polynomial Ornstein-Uhlenbeck volatility models
item.description: arXiv:2405.02170v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Fourier-Laplace transforms of a broad class of polynomial Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) volatility models, including the well-known Stein-Stein, Sch\"obel-Zhu, one-factor Bergomi, and the recently introduced quintic OU models motivated by the SPX-VIX joint calibration problem. We show the connection between the joint Fourier-Laplace functional of the log-price and the integrated variance, and the solution of an infinite-dimensional system of Riccati equations. Next, under some non-vanishing conditions on the Fourier-Laplace transforms, we establish an existence result for such Riccati equations and show how the Fourier-Laplace functional can be seen as the limit of a sequence of entire functions. On the practical side, we develop a numerical scheme to solve the stiff infinite-dimensional system of Riccati equations and demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the scheme for pricing SPX options and volatility swaps using Fourier and Laplace inversions, with specific examples of the quintic OU and the one-factor Bergomi models and their calibration to real market data.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Abi Jaber (Xiaoyuan), Shaun (Xiaoyuan), Li, Xuyang Lin

item.title: Affine Pricing Models from Group Quantization and Holonomy
item.description: arXiv:2609.28863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The analytic tractability of affine pricing models is usually expressed through two complementary formulations: a coordinate-space pricing operator and an exponential-affine transform representation governed by generalized Riccati equations. We develop \emph{Affine Holonomy Group Quantization} (AHGQ) as a geometric framework in which these two formulations arise from the same underlying structure. The construction separates the affine pricing symbol into a homogeneous quadratic sector and a complementary affine sector. The first generates a finite-dimensional symplectic transport and a centrally extended Lie group, while the second is represented by a multiplicative holonomy carried by a thin-path groupoid. Their combination determines an affine Poincar\'e--Cartan form. Its characteristic dynamics reduce in momentum variables to the generalized Riccati system and its scalar amplitude, whereas the coordinate representation recovers the standard affine pricing operator. Representative Gaussian and square-root models illustrate the construction. The contribution is structural: AHGQ gives a common geometric origin to the coordinate and transform representations of continuous-path, time-homogeneous affine pricing models.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Garcia
